title: Semantic color tokens for UI states
when: The user needs consistent colors for meaning (success, warning, danger, info, selected, disabled) across messages, badges and inputs.
prompt:
Goal: Purpose named color tokens so every message, badge and input state uses the same tested colors.
Steps:
1. List the states the UI really has: success, warning, danger, info, selected, disabled.
2. Give each three tokens: --color-danger (icons, borders), --color-danger-bg (soft tint), --color-danger-text (dark shade for text on the tint).
3. Test each -text on its -bg at 4.5 to 1, and each strong color against the page at 3 to 1.
4. Keep warning text dark: use a deep brown amber for text and bright amber only for icons.
5. Point components at tokens: .alert-danger, input[aria-invalid="true"] and .badge-danger read the same variables.
6. Pair every state color with a word or icon so it works for color blind users.
Quality bar:
- No raw hex outside :root.
- Danger and success differ in lightness, not only hue.
- Disabled uses aria-disabled and lower contrast, not color alone.
Pitfalls:
- Red and green that merge with deuteranopia.
- Yellow text on white.
- The brand accent reused as info, so links and notices blur.
Verify:
- [ ] Each state has strong, bg and text tokens.
- [ ] Tint and text pairs pass 4.5 to 1.
- [ ] Components reference the tokens.
- [ ] Messages carry text, not only color.
Output: The semantic token block in style.css and the component rules that use it.

examples.input: define colors for success, error and warning messages
